Calling `stats::fisher.test` with crafted input results in a segfault due to an out of bounds write:

```
> stats::fisher.test(matrix(300000000L, nrow = 2L, ncol = 3L))

 *** caught segfault ***
address 0xbb3e1afceb60, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: stats::fisher.test(matrix(300000000L, nrow = 2L, ncol = 3L))
An irrecoverable exception occurred. R is aborting now ...
[1]    12139 segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

The fault originates from an out of bounds write in `f2exact`, located in `fexact.c:401`, as reported by valgrind:

```
==12318== Invalid write of size 4
==12318==    at 0xBF4E300: f2xact (fexact.c:401)
==12318==    by 0xBF4E300: fexact (fexact.c:291)
==12318==    by 0xBF516CB: Fexact (fexact.c:2070)
==12318==    by 0x410265F: R_doDotCall (dotcode.c:763)
...
```

There's also a possibly related integer overflow reported by ubsan when running the same input:

```
.../R-devel/src/library/stats/src/fexact.c:1842:20: runtime error: left shift of 1800000001 by 1 places cannot be represented in type 'int'
```

Version:
```
svn rev r90590
```

OS:
```
Linux Ubuntu 26.04, aarch64
```

Also fails fataly on M1 Mac, although with a bus error.
